app.title: E-QuakeVis (Database Gempa)
app.summary: A person loads an earthquake catalogue: the bundled archive, or their own CSV or Excel file after matching its columns. They pick a date range and narrow the events by depth, magnitude, administrative region, distance to coast, faults or volcanoes, and an optional box drawn on the map or typed as coordinates. The filtered events are shown as epicentres on a layered map, as hypocentres in 3D with slab surfaces and a cross-section along a profile they draw, and as summary charts and a table. The person leaves with a CSV of the filtered events or a print-ready PNG/PDF map sheet. A hazard tab also shows probabilistic hazard grids with a hazard curve for each site, and can launch new hazard runs.

task.text: Narrow an earthquake catalogue to the events in a region, depth and magnitude range of interest, look at them in map, 3D and statistical views, and export the subset as a table or a publication map.

data.text: A catalogue of earthquake events with time, coordinates, depth and magnitude, joined with reference geography: fault traces, trenches, slab depth contours and grids, volcano hazard areas, administrative boundaries, population density, seismic stations, and gridded hazard results with hazard curves.
data.item: one earthquake event (a hypocentre with time, latitude, longitude, depth and magnitude)

stage.text: exploring and subsetting an earthquake catalogue, then mapping it for a report

mechanism.text: Sidebar filters and a drawn bounding box set one filtered event set. That set feeds every tab: the layered epicentre map, the 3D hypocentre and cross-section workspace, the statistics charts, the event table, and the publication-map renderer. Clicks on the map hide single events or focus a volcano, and picks in the 3D view and the cross-section highlight the same event in each other.

field.text: earthquake catalogue analysis and probabilistic seismic hazard in seismology

workflow.name: filter an event catalogue on a map and export the subset or a print map

steps.here: The catalogue comes from a local indexed archive by date range (the last 90 days by default). Extra CSV or Excel files can be added: pick the sheet, match columns to the required fields, preview, then append them to the database.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Sliders for depth and magnitude, multiselects for province, district and epicentre location type, and maximum distance to the coast, to chosen fault segments and to chosen volcanoes. A rectangle drawn on the map or typed coordinates keep only the events inside the box.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Epicentres are drawn on a basemap that can be switched, with optional layers for faults, trenches, slab contours, volcano hazard areas, stations and population density, plus headline counts. Clicking a point can hide that event.

In 3D, hypocentres sit with Slab2 surfaces. The person draws a profile A–A′ with a corridor width to get a depth cross-section, and an event picked in one plot is marked in the other. The events in the slice export as CSV.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Summary counts and depth histogram, magnitude against depth, top provinces and largest events. The hazard tab classifies PGA/SA grids by return period, and a click on a land site shows its hazard curve.
The filtered events download as a dated CSV. A publication sheet (template, page size, DPI, scale, logos, layers, inset) is rendered to PNG and PDF for download.

distinctive: Each event gets precomputed spatial context, including province or district, land or sea, nearest fault segment and distance to it, so the person can filter by distance to a fault, volcano or coast.
Hypocentres are viewed against subduction slab geometry, with a cross-section along a profile the person draws, to see dipping seismicity zones.
The publication sheet follows cartographic conventions: a representative scale, north arrow, locator inset, source lines, and a spatial-planning layout template.
Probabilistic hazard runs in a separate engine process and come back as classified grids by intensity measure and return period, with hazard curves for each site.
